findings.text: scope lens, medium: The unit probe of `_ccgl_read_holder` hand-writes the `run-status-comment.txt` fixture instead of calling `rsc_render_header` to generate it, violating CLAUDE.md's rule that data another part of the engine writes must be made with the writer's own code, never by hand. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh: "cat > "$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$_dscla4_issue/run-status-comment.txt" <<'RSCEOF' <!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=holder-run-99 --> <!-- zbuild-holder: run-holder-99 on machine-other --> run is in progress... RSCEOF"; happens when: When `rsc_render_header` changes the exact text of the `<!-- zbuild-holder: ... -->` comment (for example adds surrounding whitespace, renames the attribute, or changes the delimiter), `_ccgl_read_holder`'s regex silently stops matching live GitHub comments while this test continues to pass against its frozen hand-written fixture — the two diverge without any test catching it.; fix: test; ACCEPTED IF: The run-status-comment fixture used in this holder-read unit probe is generated by calling `rsc_render_header` with a known `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` value, so any change to the writer's format is immediately reflected in the test's Given condition and the test cannot silently pass while the reader is broken.)
